summary: Still worth running, and the case is stronger on the new master. In the rega profile (2910b2fb4b744865) _align_parallel_kernel is 16.9/17.1 us at turn_1 (2.3%/1.5%) and 70.3/70.9 us at turn_4 (3.1%/1.9%), so its share went up once the expert GEMMs got faster. But the change text is stale and must be re-targeted before building: the live caller is _experts_rega at REGA_BSM=16 (200<T<=4096). Marlin (bsm 64) and ssdq (bsm 128) are now fallbacks only, so compile, equivalence and gate must cover bsm 16.
justification: A: The mechanism holds and is unchanged by the merge. Master's _align_parallel_kernel (submission.py:651) runs on local_count+1 = 33 programs. Every program streams all n = 8T ids twice with a [512 x 32] compare (count pass, then place pass), so the work is about 33 x 2 x n, on 33 SMs. A two-launch count/prefix-place reads each id about twice, spread over cdiv(n,1024) programs (24 at T=3012, 6 at T=753). The 70 us down to <=10 us target at turn_4 is plausible. At turn_1 the target is 17 down to about 6-8 us: there are only 6 programs per launch there, plus a second graph node, so the saving is maybe 9-11 us. Re-based expectation on the new master: turn_4 sliding about -60 us of 2295 (~2.6%), full about -60 of 3821 (~1.6%); turn_1 sliding about -10 of 738 (~1.4%), full about -10 of 1177 (~0.9%); first_turn flat, since _experts_triton keeps moe_align_block_size at 50 us. Geomean is about +0.8%, below one run's CI (1.3075-1.3474). So it must be judged on the profile rows (the align row going from 16.9/70.3 us to the two new rows), as the hypothesis itself says. It is not a duplicate. turn-align-remap-on-side-stream-under-pooler (neutral) tried to hide the align, not shrink it. turn-align-sglang32-prenorm-triton-restack swapped in SGLang's align. Neither cut the O(33n) work. WEAKEST LINK: the stale targeting. Every parameter in the change paragraph (call sites _experts_marlin/_experts_ssdq, compile for bsm 64 and 128, gate at T=753/bsm 64 and T=3012/bsm 128) names paths that no longer run at turn_1/turn_4. _experts_rega (submission.py:2872) calls _align_parallel(local_ids, 0, LOCAL_EXPERTS, REGA_BSM=16) unconditionally. If built as written: bsm 16 is never compiled or checked in prepare (risking a JIT compile in the first timed call, or an untested variant), and the gate measures variants that are not dispatched. Second weakest: at bsm 16, cap = n+480 and n_blocks = cdiv(cap,16) = 1536 at T=3012. The block_experts / sentinel tail written by the last program of launch B is larger than at bsm 128 (BLK-looped, cheap, but the tail program must not be serial over 1536 blocks with tiny tiles).
confounders: experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 (landed, 1.3275): owns the only live T<=4096 call site (bsm 16). The align feeds rega_gather and both rega_gemm launches, and its outputs size the rega grid (rows = block_experts.shape[0]*16). Bit-identical outputs mean no numeric interaction, so any row change is the align itself. However, _rega_setup gates rega against ssdq/Marlin (REGA_GATE_RATIO 0.95) and runs a two-state replay check. Align2 must be decided in prepare BEFORE _ssdq_setup and _rega_setup, so those gates and checks run on the align that will be timed. rega wins by a wide margin, so a stale gate would not flip a path, but a failure inside rega's replay/canary would silently drop the whole 1.33x. Watch for '[rega] PATH CHOSEN' staying ON in the log.

experts-turn4-ssdq-s1b-dataptr-symbol-fix (landed): now a fallback behind rega at turn_4. The hypothesis's '[align2] lines before ssdq PATH CHOSEN' ordering must now also keep rega's PATH CHOSEN lines last (the harness reads the final lines).

stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed): introduced _align_parallel and its prepare check _align_par_setup / state['align_par_ok']. align2 is compared bit-for-bit against this kernel, so the reference is sound (it writes every element of all four outputs, including the [total,cap) sentinel and the -1 block tail, so torch.equal on torch.empty outputs will not trip on garbage). Note that _experts_rega ignores align_par_ok. If align2 hooks in only behind that flag, rega will not pick it up.

sglang-pipeline-parity, experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn, experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: first_turn / Triton path only, disjoint. No confound, provided align2 is not wired into _experts_triton.
interference: No companion is warranted. The outputs are bit-identical to master's align, so downstream kernels see identical inputs and the only expected movement is the align rows themselves, readable directly from the per-shape profile. A gain is unambiguous if the 16.9/70.3 us rows are replaced by smaller rows. A headline loss with smaller align rows would be noise (the effect is below CI). An ab-revert of rega would just re-test the stale bsm 64/128 variants on paths that are no longer shipped. A control has nothing left to isolate once the change is a single kernel swap with a per-class gate.
rules_flags: None in the design: no atomics, no host sync in the timed path, scratch cnt tensor is shape-sized (cdiv(n,1024) x 32), no value-dependent allocation, no caching of input-derived data across calls.

The ON/OFF decision is prepare-time, from synthetic routings and timing, like the existing PATH CHOSEN flags. Store it in state (e.g. state['align2_ok'][bsm]) and dispatch in _align_parallel's callers or pass state in. Do not use a module global mutated from timed-call data. As the hypothesis already says, no data_ptr gating.
open_questions: REQUIRED RE-TARGET before build: replace '_experts_marlin (bsm 64) and _experts_ssdq (bsm 128)' with '_experts_rega (REGA_BSM=16, 200<T<=4096), keeping Marlin/ssdq as fallbacks'. Compile align2 for bsm 16 (and 64, 128 if it is swapped globally). Run the torch.equal equivalence suite at bsm 16 for every listed T. Gate at T=753/bsm 16 and T=3012/bsm 16 (the classes rega dispatches: low T<=1024, high above).
Where does align2 setup run? It must be before _ssdq_setup/_rega_setup (next to _align_par_setup at submission.py:609), so rega's gate and two-state replay check exercise the timed align.
At T=753 there are only 6 chunks of 1024. Would CHUNK_A=512 (12 programs) beat 1024 for turn_1? The gate will decide, but the builder could time both.
Should first_turn's moe_align_block_size (~50 us, 0.3%) also be swapped? No. Out of scope, and align-local-parallel-first-turn was already neutral.
